paper.title_en: Large-scale fission properties with BSkG3 I : fission paths and spontaneous fission half-lives
paper.abstract_en: We present our first large-scale analysis of nuclear fission properties based on the BSkG3 energy density functional. Building on the model's unprecedented agreement with ground state observables and fission data in the actinide region, we survey nearly 3300 nuclei with $80\leq Z\leq118$, spanning the region between the predicted proton and neutron drip lines. We calculate thousands of potential energy surfaces that explicitly account for triaxial and octupole deformations. We determine the corresponding least-action fission paths using microscopic collective inertias derived consistently from BSkG3 and calculate spontaneous fission (SF) half-lives within the semiclassical WKB approximation. Our results reveal a rich diversity of fission path topologies, extending well beyond the conventional two-humped picture commonly adopted in reaction codes, and a wide variety of nuclear shapes along these paths, highlighting the limitations of exploring only one collective degree of freedom. In particular, triaxiality affects not only inner barriers in the actinide region but also outer barriers and single barriers in several regions of the superheavy nuclei. Our predicted SF half-lives follow trends similar to those of previous large-scale studies, although significant differences emerge near the neutron drip line. The resulting dataset, including fission barriers, SF half-lives, and saddle-point nuclear level densities, is available has been incorporated into the TALYS reaction code and the BRUSLIB repository. It provides a microscopic foundation for nuclear reaction calculations and astrophysical applications, particularly rapid neutron-capture simulations, which require reliable fission properties of nuclei far from the valley of stability.
